audit: 2026-09-15 scheduled remote agent (second fire of the day): one 50-question batch spanning all four modules, published as data/batches/sched_multi_topic_l3_l5_2026-09-15_b_1.json through _b_10.json, five questions per file because the MCP publish path carries file content inline and a single 345 kB file does not fit one call. Tier split 24 L3, 23 L4 and 3 L5 with no L2; module split Paediatrics 11, Obstetrics and Gynaecology 13, Psychiatry 13, Medicine 13, taking the modules to 1548/1549/1548/1549 and the bank to 6194. Cell selection: the live matrix showed L3 sitting 12.4 to 14.9 points and L4 sitting 11.4 to 13.8 points below their per-topic ideals, while L5 sat at or a hair above 5.00 per cent in every module (Paediatrics 5.010, Obstetrics and Gynaecology 5.013, Psychiatry 5.081, Medicine 5.013). A strict per-question argmax over percentage deficits is degenerate at this bank size and this is now the third consecutive fire to record it: simulated directly it put 43 of 50 questions into the L3 cells of the two LARGEST modules, allocated nothing at all to Psychiatry or Medicine, and would have widened the module spread from 2 to 27, breaking the Section 2 rule that the four modules stay within about 10 of each other. This fire therefore allocated proportionally to the positive within-topic deficits at roughly 52:48 L3 to L4, capped per-module counts to narrow the spread from 2 to 1, and placed three L5 questions in the three modules where adding 11 to 13 non-L5 questions would otherwise have dropped L5 below 5.00 per cent (Paediatrics 1, Obstetrics and Gynaecology 1, Medicine 1); Psychiatry needed none because it sat at 5.081. That is the smallest L5 allocation holding every module at or above 5.00 per cent after the batch. The routine prompt's per-question selection section should be rewritten as a proportional allocation with an explicit module-balance cap and an L5 floor rule, since that is what this and the two preceding fires have each had to reconstruct from scratch. Answer letters were deliberately rebalanced to exactly 10 per letter after an initial draft placed every correct option at A. scripts/dupe_gate.py cleared all 50 against the 6144 existing questions with zero flags. Coverage added, chosen from ground the bank had not touched: Paediatrics on toddler's fracture with a normal first radiograph, congenital nasolacrimal duct obstruction, neonatal clavicular fracture after shoulder dystocia, paediatric bacterial sinusitis identified by double sickening, trigger thumb, reflex anoxic seizure needing an electrocardiogram, primary herpetic gingivostomatitis, pubertal gynaecomastia with asymmetrical testes, balanitis xerotica obliterans, non tuberculous mycobacterial lymphadenitis and juvenile recurrent parotitis; Obstetrics and Gynaecology on cervical ectropion, trichomoniasis, cervical polyp, imperforate hymen with retention, primary dysmenorrhoea, endometrial polyp, adenomyosis in a woman trying to conceive, nipple vasospasm misdiagnosed as candida, genito-pelvic pain and penetration disorder, parvovirus B19 exposure, erosive vulval lichen planus, Sheehan syndrome and missing intrauterine device threads with an empty cavity; Psychiatry on trichotillomania, narcolepsy with cataplexy, premenstrual dysphoric disorder, mandatory notification thresholds when treating a doctor, Charles Bonnet syndrome, selective mutism, restless legs with the ferritin 75 threshold, delusional infestation, prolonged grief disorder, the cognitive impairment of depression, post stroke emotionalism, behavioural variant frontotemporal dementia and antidepressant associated hyponatraemia; Medicine on Bell palsy, acute gout in stage 4 chronic kidney disease, calcium pyrophosphate arthritis needing aspiration, venous leg ulceration and the ankle brachial index, onychomycosis confirmation before terbinafine, ocular rosacea, Meniere disease, chronic spontaneous urticaria and antihistamine updosing, valproate induced tremor, secondary syphilis mimicking pityriasis rosea, carpal tunnel syndrome with thenar wasting, adhesive capsulitis, and the HINTS examination in acute vestibular syndrome.
